# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Submitted online at my.cigna.com, or by phone at 1-800-244-6224

**From:**
Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-11 — Reference number POC-8E43F25837-44913**
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Governing policy:** *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of my hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which Cigna denied on 2026-08-11 under reference number POC-8E43F25837-44913. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision, because the clinical record in my prior authorization packet does address the plan's own criteria, and I am resubmitting that record here so nothing is missing from the file.

My surgeon, Okafor, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed. I am not asking Cigna to take that on faith — I am asking that the records already in my file be read against the plan's published guideline.

## What the plan's own policy requires, and what my records show

The plan's guideline, *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026*, states:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

and among those criteria:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

Here is how my records line up with that language.

**Femoroacetabular impingement, confirmed on imaging.** My MRI arthrogram of the hip on 2026-06-08 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The same study shows the joint space is preserved, Tonnis grade 0.

**Groin-dominant hip pain and a positive provocative exam.** My records document sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If the reviewer needs the specific test name and the measured passive internal rotation in degrees to match the wording of the criterion above, that detail is in my surgeon's office note: [office note date and the specific provocative test result and internal rotation measurement, to be supplied by Dr. Okafor's office].

**Symptoms that have not resolved on their own.** I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest.

**Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months.** My conservative care has run well past three months and has included:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, with activity modification — 18 visits completed over 8 weeks, from 2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

**No factors that would make surgery unsafe.** My records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

Because the denial was based on incomplete documentation rather than on a finding that my condition falls outside the guideline, I am asking Cigna to:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, as requested by Okafor, MD; or
2. If any single item is still considered missing, tell me in writing exactly which criterion in *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* is unmet and what document would satisfy it, so my surgeon's office can send it promptly.

I am also requesting a copy of the clinical review criteria and the reviewer's notes used to make this determination, and I ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise.

**Enclosed with this letter:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-11 (Reference POC-8E43F25837-44913)
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-08
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21 (18 visits)
- Office notes from Okafor, MD, including examination findings
- Injection record dated 2026-05-23 and medication history
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office is submitting]

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it through my.cigna.com and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed in the notice.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I am glad to provide anything further that would help complete the review.

Sincerely,

**Casey Hayes**
